item.title: 3D Printing Seattle
item.description:
3D Printing in Seattle

Future Present Labs provides engineering 3D printing in Belltown, Seattle for prototypes, fixtures, tooling, and quick validation parts. We focus on practical printed parts that help a hardware project move: workholding, assembly aids, fit-check models, protective covers, and lightweight functional components.

For manufacturing work, 3D printing is most useful when it compresses iteration. A printed nest can make an assembly step repeatable. A printed cover can prove connector clearance. A carbon-filled nylon bracket can survive enough testing to decide whether the next version should be machined.

item.title: CAD CAM Services Seattle
item.description:
CAD/CAM Services in Seattle

Future Present Labs supports Seattle CAD/CAM work for parts that need to become real hardware, not just clean screenshots. We help turn models, drawings, sketches, and revisions into machinable plans for CNC milling, turning, waterjet cutting, engraving, fixtures, and prototypes.

CAD defines the shape. CAM defines how that shape gets made. The gap between them is where many prototype delays happen: no setup face, impossible internal corners, missing tolerances, unclear threads, fragile walls, or geometry that requires a tool the schedule cannot support.

item.title: CNC Machining Eastside Seattle
item.description:
CNC Machining for Eastside Seattle Hardware Teams

Future Present Labs supports Eastside Seattle teams that need prototype and short-run CNC machining without handing the project to a distant, high-volume vendor. We work with engineers, founders, product teams, aerospace suppliers, robotics groups, and embedded hardware builders around Redmond, Kirkland, Bellevue, and the broader Puget Sound area.

The Eastside has a dense mix of hardware startups, aerospace engineering, robotics, medical device work, software-adjacent labs, and product teams that need physical parts to keep pace with design changes. A local CNC partner helps when the job needs direct engineering discussion, fast revision feedback, or practical manufacturability review before the next test.

item.title: CNC Machining Seattle
item.description:
CNC Machining in Seattle

Future Present Labs is a Seattle machine shop for prototype and short-run CNC parts. We help hardware teams, product designers, defense suppliers, event venues, and local businesses turn CAD files, drawings, or sketches into parts that are ready for test, assembly, or customer use.

Good fit projects

  • Prototype brackets, mounts, plates, adapters, and housings
  • Short-run aluminum, stainless, brass, titanium, and plastic parts
  • Fixture plates, inspection aids, drill guides, and assembly tooling
  • Iterative parts that need quick feedback from the person making them

Why work locally

Local CNC machining makes iteration faster. You can review photos, talk through tolerances, update CAD, and keep the next revision moving without shipping delays or long quoting queues.

item.title: CNC Milling Seattle
item.description:
CNC Milling in Seattle

Future Present Labs provides CNC milling in Belltown, Seattle for teams that need precise prototype parts, small production runs, and practical engineering feedback. Milling removes material with rotating cutters, so the real work is not just loading a STEP file. It is choosing setups, tools, workholding, datums, and inspection points that make the part reliable without turning the quote into a science project.

We are a strong fit when the part needs more than a file upload: tolerance review, fixture planning, material selection, revision support, or a quick conversation about what actually matters for the build.

item.title: CNC Turning Seattle
item.description:
CNC Turning in Seattle

Future Present Labs supports Seattle CNC turning projects for round parts that need accurate diameters, shoulders, bores, grooves, or threads. Turning is often the fastest and cleanest process for cylindrical geometry because the material spins while the tool forms the profile.

The best turning jobs are clear about fit: which diameter rides in a bearing, which thread mates to another part, which shoulder controls stackup, and which surface is cosmetic.

item.title: Contract Manufacturing Seattle
item.description:
Contract Manufacturing in Seattle

Future Present Labs supports contract manufacturing in Seattle for teams that need a practical local partner for parts, fixtures, small builds, and engineering-heavy production support. We are not a large factory; we are a small technical shop that is useful when the work still needs attention, context, and iteration.

That distinction matters. If you need thousands of mature parts per month, we may help with prototyping, fixtures, or supplier handoff. If you need low-volume parts, debug-heavy assemblies, or a manufacturing partner who can still talk through the design, we are a better fit.

item.title: Custom Manufacturing Seattle
item.description:
Custom Manufacturing in Seattle

Future Present Labs supports custom manufacturing projects in Seattle when the work does not fit neatly into one process. We help with mechanical parts, electronics, fixtures, engraving, assembly support, and short-run production planning.

Where we fit

  • Small-batch parts and repeat prototype runs
  • Mixed mechanical and electronics projects
  • Tooling, fixtures, and inspection aids
  • Parts that need machining, cutting, engraving, and assembly coordination

Built for practical handoffs

You can bring finished CAD, partial drawings, an existing part, or a problem statement. We will help identify the simplest manufacturing path, flag tolerance or material risks, and keep the project moving toward usable hardware.

item.title: Electronics Prototyping Seattle
item.description:
Electronics Prototyping in Seattle

Future Present Labs supports Seattle electronics prototyping when a board, sensor, fixture, or embedded product needs practical debugging and integration support. We focus on the prototype stage where the design still needs bench work, firmware, mechanical context, and test planning.

Electronics prototypes rarely fail in only one way. A schematic issue may look like firmware. A firmware issue may look like a sensor problem. A connector placed in the wrong spot can make a good board hard to use. We help work through those practical edges.

item.title: Embedded Systems Consulting Seattle
item.description:
Embedded Systems Consulting in Seattle

Future Present Labs provides embedded systems consulting in Seattle for teams building products, fixtures, sensors, controls, and test hardware. We help when firmware needs to connect to real hardware, and when the physical setup needs to support reliable testing.

Embedded projects become expensive when the team cannot see what the system is doing. Good logs, repeatable fixtures, known-good hardware, and simple test scripts can save more time than a large rewrite.

item.title: Engineering Prototyping Seattle
item.description:
Engineering Prototyping in Seattle

Engineering prototypes need to answer a technical question. Will the part fit? Will the fixture hold repeatably? Can the board survive the test? Does the firmware capture the right data? Future Present Labs helps Seattle teams build prototypes around those questions.

We are most useful when the prototype crosses domains. A machined part may need a board mount. A PCB may need a fixture. A firmware test may need a repeatable sensor position. A customer demo may need enough polish to be trusted without pretending it is final production.

item.title: Fixture Design Seattle
item.description:
Fixture Design in Seattle

Future Present Labs designs and builds fixtures in Seattle for machining, inspection, assembly, electronics testing, and repeatable prototype work. A good fixture makes the next operation faster, safer, and easier to verify.

Fixtures are how small teams buy repeatability. They locate parts the same way, protect delicate features, reduce operator judgment, and make test data easier to trust. They do not need to be elaborate; they need to remove the right uncertainty.

item.title: Hardware Prototyping Seattle
item.description:
Hardware Prototyping in Seattle

Hardware prototyping is messy because mechanical, electrical, firmware, and manufacturing decisions all affect each other. Future Present Labs helps Seattle hardware teams build the next version with enough context to avoid avoidable handoff problems.

The best hardware prototype is not necessarily the prettiest one. It is the one that exposes risk: fit, thermal behavior, signal integrity, cable routing, mounting, assembly access, power, firmware behavior, or test repeatability.

item.title: Laser Engraving Seattle
item.description:
Laser Engraving in Seattle

Future Present Labs provides MOPA fiber laser engraving and marking in Belltown, Seattle for prototypes, parts, panels, small batches, and production support. Engraving is useful when labels need to survive handling, cleaning, assembly, or field use.

A MOPA fiber laser gives more control over pulse settings than a basic marking setup, which can help with contrast, heat input, and mark quality on metals and some coated or engineered surfaces. The right settings still depend on material, finish, coating, desired contrast, and whether the mark is decorative or functional.

item.title: Part Marking Seattle
item.description:
Part Marking in Seattle

Future Present Labs provides part marking in Seattle for teams that need serial numbers, QR codes, labels, revision marks, panel text, and durable identification on prototype or short-run parts. Marking is especially useful when parts need traceability, clear assembly steps, or field-ready labels.

Industrial marking is different from decoration. The mark needs to be readable after handling, cleaning, assembly, and sometimes coating or field use. That means placement, contrast, size, orientation, and material all matter.

item.title: PCB Design Seattle
item.description:
PCB Design in Seattle

Future Present Labs helps Seattle hardware teams with PCB design, electronics prototyping, bring-up, and test integration. We are a good fit when your board needs to connect cleanly to mechanical parts, fixtures, sensors, firmware, or manufacturing workflows.

PCB support

  • Schematic capture and PCB layout
  • Board revisions for prototypes and small product runs
  • Embedded hardware bring-up and bench debugging
  • Test fixtures, harnesses, and data logging support

Integrated mechanical and electronics work

Boards rarely live alone. We can design around enclosures, panel controls, mounting constraints, cable paths, and test access, then support the surrounding CNC machining, rapid prototyping, and firmware work.

item.title: Precision Machining Seattle
item.description:
Precision Machining in Seattle

Future Present Labs provides precision machining in Seattle for parts where fit, repeatability, surface finish, and inspection notes matter. We are a small shop, which makes us a good fit for focused prototype and short-run work that benefits from direct engineering communication.

Precision machining is not the same thing as making every number tight. It means understanding which features control function, then choosing setups, cutters, datums, and checks that protect those features.

item.title: Product Prototyping Seattle
item.description:
Product Prototyping in Seattle

Future Present Labs helps Seattle teams turn product concepts into functional prototypes. We are a good fit for physical products that involve machined parts, printed fixtures, embedded electronics, panels, housings, or test hardware.

Product prototypes have different jobs at different stages. A proof-of-concept build can be ugly if it proves the core mechanism. A pilot unit needs better fit, labeling, assembly sequence, and service access. A customer demo needs the details that make people believe the product is real.

item.title: Prototype Machining Seattle
item.description:
Prototype Machining in Seattle

Prototype machining is different from production machining. The goal is to make the next test possible, learn quickly, and avoid spending time on details that do not affect the current decision. Future Present Labs helps Seattle teams machine prototype parts with that mindset.

A prototype may need production-like material, real threads, bearing fits, flatness, or stiffness. It may also only need to prove clearance, ergonomics, assembly sequence, or sensor placement. The process should match the question the prototype is supposed to answer.

item.title: Rapid Prototyping Seattle
item.description:
Rapid Prototyping in Seattle

Future Present Labs helps Seattle teams move from idea to working prototype with fewer handoffs. We combine CNC machining, 3D printing, electronics, engraving, waterjet cutting, and practical design support for projects where the next useful revision matters more than a polished process deck.

Prototype work we handle

  • First-article machined parts and fixture plates
  • Functional 3D printed tooling and assembly aids
  • Electronics prototypes, harnesses, and test rigs
  • Marked panels, labels, and short-run presentation parts

Faster iteration

Local prototyping keeps feedback loops short. We can talk through CAD, identify risky features, suggest materials, and help decide what should be machined, printed, engraved, or cut first.

item.title: Small Batch Manufacturing Seattle
item.description:
Small Batch Manufacturing in Seattle

Future Present Labs helps Seattle teams with small-batch manufacturing when the job is too real for a one-off prototype but not ready for high-volume production. This is the space where repeatability, setup notes, packaging, and revision control start to matter.

Small batches are often where a product learns how it wants to be made. The first five parts prove the design; the next 25 expose what takes too long, what needs a fixture, what should be engraved, and what needs clearer inspection criteria.

item.title: Waterjet Cutting Seattle
item.description:
Waterjet Cutting in Seattle

Future Present Labs supports WAZER abrasive waterjet cutting in Belltown, Seattle for teams that need accurate flat-pattern parts without heat-affected edges. Waterjet cutting is useful for metals, plastics, composites, rubber, gasket stock, and other materials where laser heat or mechanical cutting is a poor fit.

The WAZER is a compact abrasive waterjet platform, which makes it a strong fit for prototypes, short-run flat parts, panels, shims, gaskets, brackets, and blanks that later receive CNC finishing. It is not the right tool for every large-format or heavy-plate job; when scale or thickness exceeds the sensible range, we can help identify that early.
